verifications.claim: Francia was the largest post-Roman Germanic kingdom in Western Europe.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The Kingdom of the Franks (Latin: Regnum Francorum), also known as the Frankish Kingdom or Francia, was the largest post-Roman kingdom in Western Europe."

verifications.claim: Francia was established by Clovis I in 481 AD.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "• Established c. 481"; "Its founder was King Clovis I"
verifications.reasoning: R1 explicitly states establishment c. 481 by Clovis I.

verifications.claim: Francia spanned modern France, Germany, and surrounding areas.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Expansions into Gaul (France), "western and southern Germany", peak area 1,200,000 km² covering those regions.
verifications.reasoning: R1 describes territories matching modern France, Germany, and surroundings at peak.

verifications.claim: Francia divided into West Francia (France) and East Francia (Germany) in 843.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: "Treaty of Verdun 10 August 843"; R2: divisions into West, East, Middle Francia.
verifications.reasoning: R1 and R2 confirm 843 division into West (France), East (Germany), and Middle Francia.

verifications.claim: Francia was founded by Clovis I.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Its founder was King Clovis I"

verifications.claim: Clovis I united Frankish tribes.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Clovis I who united Frankish tribes"

verifications.claim: Clovis I expanded into Roman Gaul.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "expanded the Frankish realm into the Roman Gaul"

verifications.claim: Francia was governed by the Merovingians from 476 to 750.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: Merovingians from Clovis (c.481/509), ends 751 with Pepin; no mention of 476-750 exactly.
verifications.reasoning: Dates incorrect: starts after 476 (Clovis 481), ends 751 not 750.

verifications.claim: Francia was governed later by the Carolingians.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "ruled by the Merovingian and Carolingian dynasties"

verifications.claim: Francia reached its height under Charlemagne.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "secured the greatest expansion of the Frankish state by the early 9th century"; Charlemagne crowned 800.
verifications.reasoning: R1 attributes peak expansion to Charlemagne.

verifications.claim: Charlemagne was crowned Emperor in 800.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Charlemagne crowned Emperor of the Romans 25 December 800"

verifications.claim: Francia was divided in 843 by the Treaty of Verdun.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Treaty of Verdun 10 August 843"

verifications.claim: The Treaty of Verdun divided Francia into West Francia ruled by King Charles the Bald, East Francia ruled by King Louis the German, and Middle Francia ruled by Emperor Lothair I.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R2: West to Charles the Bald, East to Louis the German, Middle to Lothair I.
verifications.reasoning: Precise match on rulers and divisions.

verifications.claim: The Franks adopted Christianity following Clovis I.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Clovis converted 508, "put himself on good terms with... Gallo-Roman subjects"; Franks Christianized.
verifications.reasoning: Clovis's conversion led to Frankish adoption.

verifications.claim: The Latin alphabet was used alongside Romance and Germanic languages.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: Latin principal written language; R3: "The use of the Latin alphabet in,Romance/Germanic boundary"
verifications.reasoning: Latin alphabet used, with Romance/Germanic spoken; not explicit 'alongside'.

verifications.claim: The Carolingian era saw a revival in education and arts.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Carolingian Renaissance" of literate culture

verifications.claim: The Carolingian revival in education and arts occurred particularly under Charlemagne.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Charlemagne's patronage led to "Carolingian Renaissance"

verifications.claim: Charles Martel won the Battle of Tours in 732.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Charles Martel... Battle of Tours in 732"

verifications.claim: Francia was originally focused on the region between the Rhine and Seine rivers.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "core Frankish territories... close to the Rhine and Meuse rivers... as far as the Somme river"
verifications.reasoning: Rhine yes, Seine approximate (Somme near Seine), Meuse mentioned.

verifications.claim: Francia expanded to cover much of Western Europe.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Peak 1,200,000 km², expansions across Western Europe.
verifications.reasoning: Described as covering much of Western Europe.

verifications.claim: Francia is the direct predecessor to modern France (West Francia).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "West Francia came under control of the Capetian dynasty, becoming the Kingdom of France"

verifications.claim: Francia is the direct predecessor to modern Germany (East Francia).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "East Francia... becoming the Kingdom of Germany"
